meta.title: Who really said "Would You Ever Ask a Man that Question?"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Hillary Clinton really said it — to a moderator who asked which designers she prefers, at a televised town hall in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, 2 December 2010.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Would You Ever Ask a Man that Question?'?
meta.ogDescription: Verified against the State Department transcript: Bishkek, 2 Dec 2010. Asked which designers she preferred, Secretary Clinton replied — and the room applauded.

answer.label: Spoken by
answer.sourceLine: She really said it, and the exact wording survives in an official transcript. On 2 December 2010, at a televised town hall in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, a moderator asked Secretary of State Clinton which clothing designers she preferred; her reply — “Would you ever ask a man that question?” — is printed word for word in the U.S. Department of State record of the event ↗, followed by “(Laughter.) (Applause.)”

source.heading: The source

docMeta.dd: Hillary Rodham Clinton, Secretary of State
U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Public Affairs

source.excerpt:
MODERATOR 1: Okay. Which designers do you prefer?
SECRETARY CLINTON: What designers of clothes?
MODERATOR 1: Yes.
SECRETARY CLINTON: Would you ever ask a man that question? (Laughter.) (Applause.)
MODERATOR 1: Probably not. Probably not. (Applause.)
MODERATOR 2: How many hours do you sleep?
SECRETARY CLINTON: That’s my answer.
MODERATOR 1: Yeah, I got it. I got it. That was a tough one.
trail: Went to the primary record first: the U.S. Department of State transcript of the Bishkek townterview ↗, dated 2 December 2010, which prints the exchange verbatim including the laughter and applause cues.

Checked the specialist: Quote Investigator ↗ examined the quotation on 6 September 2012 and concluded “the quotation is accurate, and the interaction took place in 2010 in Kyrgyzstan,” footnoting the same transcript.

Confirmed the placement on Wikiquote ↗, where the exchange sits in the sourced body of her quotations from her years as Secretary of State — not among the attributed or misattributed entries — cited to the State Department transcript.

Traced the spread through the Yahoo News report of 15 August 2012 ↗, which quotes the transcript and records that the excerpt had just been reposted by Boston Review and shared thousands of times on Tumblr, Twitter and Facebook.
source.excerptNote: Moments earlier the same moderator had introduced this closing round as “not just silly questions,” and Clinton had answered: “Oh, I’ve never been asked a silly question in my entire life. (Laughter.)” The transcript names three Kyrgyz hosts on the panel but labels the questioners only as MODERATOR 1 and MODERATOR 2, so it does not record which of them asked about the designers.

author.name: Hillary Rodham Clinton
author.heading: Who said it
author.metaLine: b. 1947 · U.S. Secretary of State 2009–2013 · Senator, First Lady, presidential nominee
author.bio: Born Hillary Diane Rodham in Chicago in 1947, she trained as a lawyer before becoming First Lady of the United States, then a U.S. Senator from New York, and then the 67th Secretary of State. The Bishkek remark comes from the middle of that last job, on a swing through Central Asia. Her impatience with the fashion question was not a one-off pose: minutes earlier in the same conversation, advising a young Kyrgyz law student, she had observed that “when a man walks into a courtroom it’s rare for someone to say, ‘Oh, look what he is wearing’” — but that a woman will be noticed.

misattribution.heading: What gets told wrong
misattribution.intro: The unusual thing about this one is that the attribution is right and almost everything around it is wrong. The line is genuine; what fell off in transit was the date, the country, the setting and the fact that a transcript exists at all — which is exactly why so many people assumed it was made up.

items.why: The version that circulated on Facebook had her rebuking a reporter who asked about fashion “while visiting some country in Central Asia” — the wording of the query that prompted Quote Investigator’s 2012 check ↗. The record shows something friendlier and more specific: a youth town hall in Bishkek co-hosted by Kyrgyz public TV and the American University of Central Asia, where a moderator had already flagged the closing round as light-hearted.

Because it spread without a citation, the default assumption became fabrication — Quote Investigator filed the reader’s query under the header “Hillary Clinton? Apocryphal?” ↗ before resolving it as accurate. Doubt is the right instinct with a famous-name quote; here it happens to be misplaced.

Detached from its transcript the line reads like campaign-trail material, but she was not campaigning. The State Department record ↗ identifies the speaker as “Hillary Rodham Clinton, Secretary of State,” on a diplomatic visit in December 2010.

misattribution.truthLine: She said it on 2 December 2010, in Bishkek, as Secretary of State, to a town-hall moderator who asked which designers she preferred — and you can read the full exchange in the official transcript ↗.

context.heading: Why it stuck
lead: The line travels because of what surrounds it. This was not a hostile press conference — it was the friendly, wind-down round of a youth town hall broadcast on Kyrgyz public television, and the moderator had teed it up by apologising in advance for questions that were “not just silly.” Clinton had already batted that away: “Oh, I’ve never been asked a silly question in my entire life.” Then came the designers.

Her answer refuses the premise rather than the questioner, and the transcript records the room agreeing with her: laughter, applause, and the moderator conceding “Probably not. Probably not.” When the next question arrived she was still on the point — “That’s my answer,” she said, letting the silence do the work.
context.detailsSummary: How a 2010 transcript became a 2012 meme
detailsBody: The exchange sat quietly in the State Department archive for well over a year. It resurfaced in August 2012 after Boston Review reposted it; on 15 August 2012 Yahoo News’s The Ticket reported that the excerpt “has been shared thousands of times on Tumblr, Twitter and Facebook” ↗.

What spread was the four-line exchange, usually stripped of date, country and setting. Within weeks a reader wrote to Quote Investigator saying they had seen it on Facebook, that “no details were given about when or where,” and asking straightforwardly whether it was a real quote ↗. It is a useful reminder that a quotation can be perfectly genuine and still end up looking invented, purely because nobody carried the citation along with it.
context.pull: “Probably not. Probably not.” — the moderator, conceding, on the transcript

sourcesVerified.claim: The official State Department transcript of the 2 December 2010 Bishkek townterview contains the exact exchange, including "Would you ever ask a man that question? (Laughter.) (Applause.)", the moderator's "Probably not. Probably not.", the follow-up "That's my answer.", the earlier "Oh, I've never been asked a silly question in my entire life.", and the courtroom remark about what a man wears; it is headed "Remarks, Hillary Rodham Clinton, Secretary of State, KTR Studio, Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, December 2, 2010" and names Kaarmanbek Kuluev, Kadyr Toktogulov and Elvira Sarieva while labelling the questioners only MODERATOR 1 / MODERATOR 2.

Quote Investigator, published 6 September 2012, concludes "the quotation is accurate, and the interaction took place in 2010 in Kyrgyzstan", reprints the transcript passage, footnotes the State Department transcript, and records the reader query as having seen it on Facebook with "No details ... about when or where", describing her as "asked by a reporter about fashion" while "visiting some country in Central Asia", under the header "Hillary Clinton? Apocryphal?"

Wikiquote carries the exchange verbatim in the sourced body of Hillary Clinton quotations, in the Secretary of State (2009–2013) section rather than the Attributed or Misattributed sections, cited to the "Townterview Hosted by KTR" transcript dated December 2, 2010.

Yahoo News's The Ticket, dated August 15, 2012, quotes the transcript exchange and states that it was "posted on Tuesday by Boston Review" and "has been shared thousands of times on Tumblr, Twitter and Facebook", and that the town hall was organised by the American University in Central Asia and the U.S. Embassy in Kyrgyzstan and broadcast on public television there, with the designer question prefaced by the moderator as "silly".

The U.S. Department of State Copyright Information page states verbatim: "Unless a copyright is indicated, information on State Department websites is in the public domain and may be copied and distributed without permission. Citation of the U.S. State Department as source of the information is appreciated."

The official U.S. Department of State YouTube channel hosts video of the full event, titled "Secretary Clinton Participates in a Townterview in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan", described as a "townterview hosted by KTR in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on December 2, 2010".
Hillary Diane Rodham was born October 26, 1947 in Chicago, Illinois, and served as United States Secretary of State from January 21, 2009 to February 1, 2013.
A BuzzFeed piece on Sheryl Sandberg references the 2010 Kyrgyzstan exchange, quoting Clinton's "Would you ever ask a man that question?" and the interviewer's "Probably not. Probably not."
